from .core import wrap_text

__all__ = ['wrap_text']
----
def _wrap_paragraph(words, width):$
    lines = []$
    cur = ""$
    for w in words:$
        if len(w) > width:$
            if cur:$
                lines.append(cur)$
                cur = ""$
            while len(w) > width:$
                lines.append(w[:width])$
                w = w[width:]$
            cur = w  # final chunk starts the new current line$
        elif not cur:$
            cur = w$
        elif len(cur) + 1 + len(w) <= width:$
            cur += " " + w$
        else:$
            lines.append(cur)$
            cur = w$
    if cur:$
        lines.append(cur)$
    return lines$
$
$
def wrap_text(text: str, width: int) -> str:$
    if width < 1:$
        raise ValueError("width must be >= 1")$
    paragraphs = []$
    current = []$
    for line in text.split("\n"):$
        if line == "":$
            if current:$
                paragraphs.append(current)$
                current = []$
        else:$
            current.extend(line.split())$
    if current:$
        paragraphs.append(current)$
    blocks = ["\n".join(_wrap_paragraph(words, width)) for words in paragraphs]$
    return "\n".join(blocks)$

"`, so the blank line between paragraphs was lost, and it now joins them with `"

"`. The paragraph splitting already collapsed runs of blank lines into one separator, so that behavior is unchanged. I did not touch `tests/`, add dependencies, or change the public API. Spot checks on a few edge cases (empty input, blank-only input, a long word, and a mix of blank and non-blank lines) gave sensible output.
